## TL;DR

Task #1075 adds an installed-versus-running version signal to RepoOS, lets supervised servers restart through their supervisor, provides a safe manual fallback when there is no supervisor, and exposes restart-now and restart-when-idle actions in the dashboard. The round 1 review caught two restart coordination bugs and a CLI failure mode. Those are fixed, and focused route and upgrade-message tests now exercise the reported cases.

## Work and rationale

The server reports the version captured from its own build at process start and reads the installed build marker from disk through a short cache. The dashboard can therefore distinguish a release that is merely available from an upgrade already installed on disk while the current server process is still old. The status also includes running agent and check counts and whether a known supervisor can bring the process back after exit.

The UI presents the running and installed versions, active work, and the restart options. A user can restart immediately, queue the restart until idle, or dismiss the notice for that installed version. Restart requests use the server's supervisor-aware restart path; an unsupervised process returns a conflict with the manual command instead of being terminated without a restart path. The upgrade command also checks for a running server after replacing the installed files and prints a one-line reminder when the server is still on another version.

Review round 1 found that the pre-existing `/api/server/restart` and the new installed-upgrade endpoint had begun sharing one module-level idle timer. Their callbacks had different restart behavior, so whichever request created the timer first controlled what happened. I removed idle scheduling from the pre-existing endpoint. The installed-upgrade route now owns the idle timer and its callback exclusively, while the original restart route retains its reload behavior.

The restart action in the dashboard previously set its busy latch and never released it. The request's `finally` now clears that latch, including after failure or cancellation, so the controls remain usable after any response. The delayed status refresh still runs to observe a replacement server reconnecting.

The CLI's `--when-idle` polling previously treated a failed request as if the server had become idle. It now checks for a successful HTTP response and numeric agent/check counts. If it cannot establish the state, it prints an error and returns before invoking the destructive restart path. This favors a clear retry over restarting while work may still be active.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the existing restart route and its callers to determine why two different when-idle requests could collide. A single shared coordinator could have preserved both request styles, but would require defining which action wins when a reload restart and an installed-upgrade process restart overlap. The narrower change was to leave the existing reload route's behavior intact and give the installed-upgrade route sole ownership of its timer.

For the CLI reminder, I extracted the line formatting into `upgradeRestartReminder`. That keeps the command's output testable without running an actual package upgrade or contacting a server. For server status, I added a route test with a fake installed version and fake supervisor detection, and exercised the unsupervised refusal response. Existing `server-restart` tests cover supervisor restart and injected stop/respawn behavior.

## Challenges and blockers

The required scoped check initially tried multiple remote validation hosts, but each failed RepoOS's link probe. RepoOS then queued the local gate behind another serialized check. I left the check running and waited for the local fallback rather than interpreting host connectivity as a code failure.

The first run of the new route test exposed that the running build in this worktree was newer than the fake disk version. The test fixture was adjusted to use a version above the actual running version, which makes the restart-pending assertion meaningful instead of depending on a stale version literal.

## Key learnings

Idle restart state must have one owner when its eventual action can vary; sharing only the timer while keeping per-request callbacks creates order-dependent behavior. A destructive action should fail closed if its safety poll fails, even if retrying indefinitely would be another reasonable policy. Finally, restart UI busy state must be cleared independently from reconnection polling, since a request error or an accepted asynchronous restart should not permanently disable the user controls.

Focused tests passed for the new status/refusal route and the CLI reminder. The UI production build completed. The final scoped RepoOS check is the remaining verification gate for this report draft; its result should be bound by RepoOS during handoff finalization.
